---
title: "Command line"
---

`dofjson` is a console script; `dofjson --help` lists every option. With no
option, it queries one date. The files it downloads go to `--outdir`
(default: `output/`).

## Querying a date

```bash
dofjson 2026-07-16 --endpoint notas --outdir output
```

`date` is the positional argument, formatted `YYYY-MM-DD`; it is ignored with
`--nota` and `--archivo`. `--endpoint` picks which date-based SIDOF service to
query: `diario` (the day's editions), `notas` (the default: the day's legal
provisions) or `indicadores` (exchange rate, TIIE, UDIS). `--outdir` sets
where the JSON is saved.

A day that SIDOF reports as empty is put to the DOF website before it is
written off, and the saved JSON records the source in its `fuente` key; the
`--respaldo` option below controls that. A date already in the local cache is
read off disk instead (`--cache-dir`).

```bash
dofjson 1999-03-08 --endpoint notas      # a day SIDOF lost: "fuente": "dof.gob.mx"
```

## One legal provision

```bash
dofjson --nota 4997808
dofjson --nota-imagenes 4997808
dofjson --nota-pdf 4997808
```

`--nota` downloads a single legal provision by its `codNota` alone: it saves
its JSON when it carries `cadenaContenido` (its HTML text), and falls back to
its scanned page image otherwise. `--nota-imagenes` downloads the scanned page
image(s) whether or not the provision also has HTML content. `--nota-pdf`
downloads the provision as its own PDF: the whole edition PDF sliced down to
the provision's pages.

## A whole edition

```bash
dofjson --pdf-edicion 16-06-2026 --edicion VES --outdir output
dofjson --pdf-diario 123456
dofjson --imagenes-diario 123456
dofjson --imagen NOMBRE_ARCHIVO --edicion MAT
```

`--pdf-edicion` downloads the PDF of a whole edition from its date
(`DD-MM-YYYY`) and `--edicion` (`MAT`, `VES` or `EXT`), resolving the
`codDiario` first; `--edicion` is required with it. `--pdf-diario` does the
same when you already have the edition's `codDiario`, which a legal
provision's `get_nota` response carries along with `pagina` and
`paginaHasta`. `--imagenes-diario` lists the per-page scanned images of an
edition by its `codDiario`. `--imagen` downloads one scanned page as a JPEG by
its `nombreArchivo`, as listed by `--imagenes-diario`; it requires
`--edicion`.

## The archive

```bash
dofjson --archivo
dofjson --archivo --desde 1980-01-01 --hasta 1980-12-31 --pausa 1.0
dofjson --archivo --respaldo todos --cache-dir cache
```

`--archivo` downloads the daily legal-provisions index of a whole date range
into a resumable local archive, one JSON per day. `--desde` and `--hasta` bound
the range (`YYYY-MM-DD`; by default from 1917-01-02 to today), and `--pausa`
is the number of seconds to wait between requests (default 0.5). With
`--archivo`, `--outdir` defaults to `notas-archivo/`. The details, the
directory layout and how it resumes are on the [Archive](archive.qmd) page.

`--respaldo` decides what to do when SIDOF reports a day as empty: `habiles`
(the default) re-checks Monday to Friday against the DOF website, `todos` also
re-checks weekends, and `nunca` trusts SIDOF alone. It applies to `--archivo`
and to a single `--endpoint notas` query. See
[the days SIDOF loses](archive.qmd#the-days-sidof-loses).

`--cache-dir` names a directory already holding `notas-archivo` assets (see
[Titles](titles.qmd)): a date already published there is read off disk instead
of querying SIDOF or the website. Left out, it is `dofjson.titulos.CACHE_DIR`;
`--cache-dir none` always fetches live. It applies to `--archivo` and to a
single `--endpoint notas` query.
